div.head: II Cn 30.7
div.ab: And gif man þone hlaford teo, þæt he be his ræde út hleope ⁊ ær unriht worhte, nime him V getrywe to ⁊ beo him sylf syxta ⁊ ladige hine þæs.
And gif man þonne hlaford teo, þæt he be his ræde ut hleope ⁊ ær unrihtes worhte, nyme him fife triwe to ⁊ beo him sylf sixta ⁊ ladige hine þæs.
Et si dominus compelletur, quod eius consilio fugerit et antea malum fecerit, assumat secum V credibiles et idem sit sextus et inde se purget.
And gyf mon ðone laford teo, þæt he be his ræde ut léope ⁊ ær unriht worhte, nime him fif getreowe men tó ⁊ beo him sylf sixta ⁊ ladige hine ðæs.
And gif man þone hlaford teo, þæt he be his ræde ut hleope and ær unriht worhte, nime him V getrywe to and beo him sylf syxta and ladige hine þæs.

Und wenn der Herr beschuldigt wird, dass auf seinen Rath jener entflohen sei und vorher Missethat verübt habe, so wähle er sich fünf Vertrauenswürdige (Männer B) [als Eideshelfer] hinzu und sei selbst Sechster und schwöre sich davon rein.

And if the lord is accused of the man having escaped on his advice and of having done wrong before, let him take five trustworthy (men, B) [as oath-helpers] and be himself the sixth, and clear himself of it.
And if the lord is accused of advising the man who had done wrong to escape, he shall choose five trustworthy men, and shall himself make a sixth, and shall clear himself of the accusation.

And if the lord is then accused that it was by his advice that he ran away, having previously committed a crime, he is to take with him five trustworthy men and be himself the sixth, and clear himself of it.

And if the lord is accused of providing advice to the person who had previously committed a crime so that he escapes, he must name five trustworthy witnesses and himself make a sixth, and exonerate himself of this.
div.note: “men” added only in the Corpus MS. Probably the original had “thegns”, as in Ethelred’s law.
getrywe to: getreowe men to B
